svg.aria-label: How I work. Rule 01, show the why. Rule 02, enforce it on the server. Rule 03, prove it, then say what's missing. Every write in Grove HRMS takes one path: interface, server action, permission check, Zod validation, transaction, audit log, Postgres.

g.text: Scores and decisions come with their reasons:

Permissions are checked where the data is
written, so hiding a button is never the only
Claims ship with tests (unit, end-to-end, axe),

svg.text: Every write in Grove HRMS takes this path, and it is traced on the server.

g.text: The browser submits a form. Nothing it sends is trusted.
A Next.js server action receives it and authenticates the session.
Role, scope and record are checked on the server; hiding a button is never the only safeguard.
The input is validated with Zod before anything is written.
The change, its audit entries and notifications commit or roll back together.
Every change records who did what, and when.
Postgres via Prisma, with row level security on and no public access.
One audited, transactional write: it all landed together, or none of it did.
